items.title: xorbitsai/inference v4.0.0

extra.evidence: # What's new in 4.0.0 (2026-10-10) ## Highlights Xinference 4.0 brings Xavier to more inference engines, enables heterogeneous prefill/decode deployments across engines and hardware, and lets you reconfigure running models without reloading their weights. - **Xavier across vLLM, SGLang, and MLX.** Xavier now supports all three engines, extending prefix KV cache sharing across compatible replicas. Reuse previously computed context across requests and replicas to avoid repeated prefill work. - **Cross-engine and cross-hardware P/D separation.** Run prefill and decode with different inference engines, including vLLM ↔ SGLang and bidirectional NVIDIA ↔ Apple silicon deployments. Choose engines and hardware independently for each role through Xinference’s unified serving interface. - **Reload engines without reloading model weights.** Opt-in GPU weight caching lets vLLM and SGLang retain weights while rebuilding the inference engine. Adjust supported concurrency, context, memory, and CUDA graph settings while preserving the model UID. - **Distributed vLLM V1 inference.** Combine tensor and pipeline parallelism across Xinference workers through the xoscar executor, with improved pipeline scheduling and failure handling. - **One-command installation and service management.** Install and start Xinference on Linux, macOS, and Windows in an isolated Python environment. Optional system services support background operation and automatic startup, with rollback for failed managed service…

items.title: Learn2Play Bench: How Well Do LLM Agents Learn from Experience in Unfamiliar Environments?
items.summary: Learning from experience is essential for LLM agents to adapt to unfamiliar and dynmaic environments. Evaluating this ability is therefore important for understanding how effectively agents acquire and use new knowledge. Existing benchmarks have sought to evaluate this ability, but they primarily evaluate tasks whose rules are provided in the instructions or already familiar to pretrained models, making it difficult to distinguish learning from interactions from reasoning with existing knowledge. items.title: nanoMuse: An Open-Source Personal Agent for Every Device You Own
items.summary: Assistants from 2011 answered and waited, and agents from 2023 did a task and stopped. In September 2026 Meta's Muse showed an agent for one person, with accounts, devices, memory and a conversation that lasts, closed, in a vendor's cloud, in one country. Such an agent is expected to act on a person's accounts and devices, remember them across weeks, speak first when it is worth it, and answer for what it did. It is a kind of software, not a model, and until now had no open counterpart. This report defines the personal agent in five questions and three horizons. It reads how Muse is built fro…

items.title: Rethinking Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation: From Alignment Coverage to Supervision Reliability
items.summary: On-Policy Distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own generations using teacher feedback. With different tokenizers, comparing teacher and student predictions requires alignment at both sequence and vocabulary levels. In this paper, we examine whether expanding this alignment coverage improves learning. Across three heterogeneous teacher--student pairs on mathematical reasoning and code generation, strict 1:1 groups already cover most student-generated tokens despite substantial vocabulary mismatch. items.title: TRACE: Rollout-Guided Quantization-Aware Training for FP4 Reinforcement Learning of MoE Language Models
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) for post-training large language models (LLMs) incurs substantial computation and memory overhead during rollout generation, which motivates low-precision rollout for efficient RL training. However, existing FP4 RL methods suffer from a key limitation: they primarily optimize quantization accuracy on the training and rollout paths independently rather than directly reducing the discrepancy between the two quantized execution paths. items.title: UltraText Bench: A Comprehensive Bilingual Benchmark for Evaluating Visual Text Rendering in Image Generation
items.summary: Dense visual text requires image generators to reproduce long strings across multiple regions with correct placement and legibility. As short-string rendering improves, evaluation must test sustained performance across more demanding scenes. We introduce UltraText Bench, a bilingual benchmark for prompt-only generation of dense visual text. It contains 432 prompts spanning 24 real-world scene categories and three difficulty levels, split equally between English and Chinese.
